verified.description:
Verified is false for an SMS or email-address channel until
its contact confirmed a code; such a channel gets no alerts.

isDefault.description:
IsDefault channels get the alerts of monitors without their own
alert settings.

verified.description:
Verified is false for an SMS or email-address channel until
its contact confirmed a code; such a channel gets no alerts.

uptimePercent.description:
UptimePercent is (ok + warning) / (ok + warning + critical); absent
without conclusive checks, and for SSL and domain monitors (no
uptime: their downtime is always 0).

chain.description:
Chain is what the server presented, leaf first; absent on results
recorded before chains were kept.

dnsNames.description: DNSNames are the subject alternative names (SANs).

fingerprintSha256.description: FingerprintSHA256 is the SHA-256 of the certificate (DER), hex.

verifiedChainLength.description:
VerifiedChainLength counts the certificates from the leaf to a
trusted root, root included; absent when the chain doesn't verify.

incidentId.description: IncidentID is absent for an alert outside an incident.

status.description: Status: pending (queued or waiting to retry), sent, dead (gave up).

code.description: Code is the AWS region code, as results' region carries it.

name.description: Name is the city people know the region by.

responseTimeMs.description:
ResponseTimeMs and SlowThresholdMs: a slow response's time and the
threshold it went over (slow_response only).

thresholdDays.description: ThresholdDays is the smallest expiry threshold the expiry is within.

date.description: Date is the UTC day, YYYY-MM-DD.

downtimeMinutes.description:
DowntimeMinutes estimates the time spent down: the share of
critical checks among the conclusive ones times the minutes the
day's checks cover. A warning is not downtime.

noData.description: NoData: no checks that day (draw it gray, never as up).

checkedAt.description:
CheckedAt is when the registry was asked (lookups are cached up to
an hour).

daysRemaining.description: DaysRemaining is 0 on the expiry day, negative after it.

dnssec.description:
DNSSEC: signed when the registry holds DS records for the domain;
absent when the registry doesn't say.

expiresAt.description:
ExpiresAt is the expiry date at 00:00 UTC; absent when the registry
publishes none.

nameservers.description:
Nameservers are the delegation's nameservers, lower case, in the
registry's order; [] when unknown (results recorded before they were
kept, registries that publish none).

registeredAt.description:
RegisteredAt is the registration (creation) date at 00:00 UTC, and
UpdatedAt the registry's last change of it; absent when the registry
doesn't publish them (and for dns answers).

statusCodes.description:
StatusCodes are the EPP status codes (RFC 5731), e.g. ok,
clientTransferProhibited, serverHold, pendingDelete,
redemptionPeriod; [] when unknown (dns answers).

thresholdsDays.description: ThresholdsDays are the expiry warnings, in days before expiry.

certificateExpiry.description:
CertificateExpiry and DomainExpiry are the watches that are on;
absent when off.

CertificateExpiry watches the expiry of the certificate the URL
presents (https:// URLs only), judged with every check; omit it to
leave the watch off.

domainExpiry.description:
DomainExpiry watches the registration of the URL's registrable
domain (shop.example.com watches example.com), looked up twice a
day; omit it to leave the watch off. Not for IP addresses.

keyword.description: Keyword is looked for in the first 256 KiB of the response body.

aspect.description: Aspect is what the incident is about.

condition.description:
Condition is what the latest check that changed the incident found;
summary is its message, facts its facts.

durationSeconds.description: DurationSeconds is how long it lasted (or has lasted so far).

monitorVariant.description:
MonitorVariant names what the monitor does, as on monitor rows
(keyword for an HTTP monitor with a keyword).

severity.description:
Severity is the current one; peakSeverity the worst it reached (a
de-escalated incident stays open at warning).

title.description:
Title names the problem in the monitor type's words (an expiry's
days counted now, or when it ended).
title.example: Certificate of example.com expires in 5 days

alertId.description:
AlertID is the alert this delivery sends: an alert goes to every
channel of its route, one delivery each.

nextAttemptAt.description: NextAttemptAt is when a pending delivery is tried again.

queuedAt.description:
QueuedAt is when the alert was queued: the time of the timeline
entry that sent it (opened, escalated, threshold, reminder).

acknowledgedByName.description:
AcknowledgedByName names who acknowledged it (their name, else
email); absent when nobody did or Norcube Auth couldn't say.

aspect.description: Aspect is what the incident is about.

condition.description:
Condition is what the latest check that changed the incident found;
summary is its message, facts its facts.

durationSeconds.description: DurationSeconds is how long it lasted (or has lasted so far).

monitorVariant.description:
MonitorVariant names what the monitor does, as on monitor rows
(keyword for an HTTP monitor with a keyword).

severity.description:
Severity is the current one; peakSeverity the worst it reached (a
de-escalated incident stays open at warning).

title.description:
Title names the problem in the monitor type's words (an expiry's
days counted now, or when it ended).
title.example: Certificate of example.com expires in 5 days

mttrLast30dSeconds.description:
MttrLast30dSeconds is the mean time to resolve of those incidents;
absent when none was resolved.

resolvedLast30d.description:
ResolvedLast30d counts incidents resolved in the last 30 days, the
ones mttrLast30dSeconds averages.

resolvedLast7d.description: ResolvedLast7d counts incidents resolved in the last 7 days.

aspects.description:
Aspects are the monitor's watched aspects (an HTTP monitor's
certificate and domain watches that are on), on list rows too; []
without watches.

condition.description: Condition explains status; absent while pending.

history.description:
History is set on list rows with include=history: the newest
results (at most 60), newest first; [] for a monitor never checked.

last24h.description:
Last24h is set on list rows of monitors that track uptime (HTTP):
the last 24 full hours plus the current one. SSL and domain monitors
show days left (condition.facts) instead.

overallStatus.description:
OverallStatus is the worst of status and the statuses of the
monitor's watched aspects (critical, warning, pending, ok), paused
while disabled. The list status filter and sort use it.

parentResource.description:
ParentResource is set when the monitor belongs to a resource of
another Norcube service ("domainradar:saved_domain:example.com"). It
can't be deleted here, and its domain can't change.

regions.description:
Regions are where the monitor is checked from, on list rows too.
Today every monitor is checked from the one region the service runs
in; with probes in more regions (planned) a monitor may list
several. Each result says which region checked it (region).

status.description:
Status is the primary aspect's: the severity of the last conclusive
check, pending before one, paused while disabled. An inconclusive
check (a failed registry lookup) never changes it.

variant.description:
Variant is what the monitor does in one word, on list rows too
(which carry no settings): keyword for an HTTP monitor that looks for
a keyword in the body, otherwise the type.

applicableEvents.description:
ApplicableEvents are the events monitors of this type can send
(offer only these in a routing form).

alertedThresholds.description:
AlertedThresholds are the expiry thresholds already alerted for the
current expiry, oldest first; [] before the first (or once renewed).

checkedAt.description:
CheckedAt is the last observation, conclusive or not; absent before
the first.

condition.description:
Condition explains status ("ok", "cert_expiring", "domain_expired",
...); absent while pending.

daysRemaining.description:
DaysRemaining is counted when read from expiresAt, negative once
expired.

message.example: certificate expires in 12 days (2026-11-12), within the 14-day threshold

subject.description:
Subject is what the aspect is about: the URL's host for the
certificate, its registrable domain for the domain.

alertWindowStart.description:
AlertWindowStart is when the largest threshold is crossed (notAfter
minus it): shade from here to notAfter.

daysRemaining.description:
DaysRemaining counts from now (certificate.daysRemaining from the
check).

nextThresholdDays.description:
NextThresholdDays / NextThresholdAt: the next threshold to cross
and when; absent once past the smallest.

thresholdsDays.description:
ThresholdsDays are the SSL monitor's expiry thresholds, largest
first; empty for an HTTP monitor (no expiry alerts).

alertedThresholds.description:
AlertedThresholds are the expiry thresholds already alerted for the
current expiry (SSL and domain monitors), oldest first; [] otherwise.
An HTTP monitor's watched certificate and domain have theirs on
aspects.

code.description:
Code is the condition ("ok", "slow_response", "cert_expiring", ...),
worded per monitor type by the dashboard.

conclusiveAt.description:
ConclusiveAt is when a check last confirmed it; older than
lastCheck.at when the newest checks couldn't tell.

message.example: certificate expires in 5 days (2026-11-05), within the 7-day threshold

since.description: Since is when the status began (statusSince).

intervalSeconds.description:
The org's plan can require more than the 30-second floor (60 s by
default), and domain monitors run at most hourly (3600); the error
message names the minimum.

checkResultId.description: CheckResultID is the check that saw it.

type.description:
Type: certificate_renewed, a check saw a certificate other than the
newest one so far, expiring later (SSL monitors and HTTP monitors
that watch their certificate; an older certificate, say from a node
behind on renewals, is not one).

uptimePercent.description:
UptimePercent is (ok + warning) / (ok + warning + critical); absent
without conclusive checks and for SSL and domain monitors.

checkResultId.description:
CheckResultID is the result that made the change (raw results are
kept about 30 days, changes a year).

condition.description: Condition is what the check that made the change found.

durationSeconds.description:
DurationSeconds is how long the status lasted (until now for the
newest change).

endedAt.description:
EndedAt is when the next change happened; absent for the newest
change (the current status, unless the monitor is paused).

events.description:
Events are what else happened while this status lasted (from
changedAt to endedAt), newest first: certificate renewals. [] when
nothing did.

p50Ms.description:
P50Ms and P95Ms approximate the window's median and 95th percentile
response time (the checks-weighted mean of the hourly percentiles).

uptimePercent.description:
UptimePercent is (ok + warning) / (ok + warning + critical): a
warning still answered, an inconclusive check counts neither way.
WarningPercent is the warnings' share of the conclusive checks.

data.description:
Data holds stable facts about the error ("limit"), the same ones gRPC
sends as ErrorInfo metadata.

detail.description: Detail is an English sentence for people.

errors.description: Errors lists the field problems of a VALIDATION_FAILED problem.

instance.description:
Instance identifies this occurrence: the request id the server
generated, also sent as X-Request-ID and logged as request_id.

reason.description: Reason is a finer stable cause within Code, when there is one.

type.description:
Type identifies the problem type (one per code); it may be
dereferenced for documentation.

field.description:
Field is the pointer of the other field: min and max compared with a
field, exclusive, dependsOn.

info.description: Uptime, SSL certificate and domain expiry monitoring.
info.title: Norcube PulseCheck API

get.description: The organization's alert channels, newest first. Credentials are never returned.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

post.description: Creates a channel. A webhook's signing secret (Standard Webhooks, whsec_…) is returned this once; SMS channels get no alerts until their number is verified. Voice-call channels can't be created, nor SMS channels where no SMS provider is configured: 400 with reason CHANNEL_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE.

400.description: Invalid fields (VALIDATION_FAILED), reason CHANNEL_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE when the kind isn't offered

403.description: Forbidden, or channel limit reached (LIMIT_REACHED), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

delete.description: Deletes the channel and removes it from every monitor's alert settings. Pending alerts to it are dropped.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: One alert channel: kind, name, whether it is a default channel, enabled and verified, and its settings without credentials (a Slack or Discord URL as a hint, a webhook's signing secret never).

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

patch.description: Changes the given fields. signingSecret is returned when a webhook's secret was rotated or replaced. A voice channel can be renamed but not enabled or given settings (400, reason CHANNEL_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE).

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: Every alert given to this channel, newest first (kept 90 days): the event and monitor (and incident), status (pending: queued or waiting to retry; sent; dead: given up), attempts, the next attempt while pending, and the last error with URLs, email addresses, phone numbers and token-like strings removed. status=dead lists the failures nobody saw.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

post.description: Sends a test alert right away and returns the provider's reference. Rate limited; an SMS counts toward the daily SMS limit. Refused while the organization is blocked for unpaid invoices.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

409.description: The provider refused it, the contact isn't verified, or a voice channel (CHANNEL_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE)

post.description: Texts (or, for an email-address channel, emails) a 6-digit code valid for 10 minutes. At most once a minute; an SMS counts toward the daily SMS limit.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

409.description: Nothing to verify, already verified, a code was just sent, or a voice channel (CHANNEL_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE)

post.description: Verifies the channel's number with the code sent. Five wrong codes (or an expired one) need a new code.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: The organization's incidents: open ones first (critical, then warning), then resolved ones, newest first within each. Filter by status (open, resolved), monitor, severity (an open incident's current severity, a resolved one's peak), aspect, acknowledged, q (part of the monitor's name or target, any case, at most 100 characters) and when it started (from inclusive, to exclusive). Every filter given must match. Rows carry the monitor's name, type, variant and target. An invalid filter is a VALIDATION_FAILED problem with the parameter's pointer ("/severity").

parameters.description:
Acknowledged: true for incidents someone acknowledged, false for
the others.
parameters.name: acknowledged

parameters.description: Aspect is what the incident is about.
parameters.name: aspect

parameters.description:
From and To bound when the incident started: from inclusive, to
exclusive (RFC 3339).
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Q is part of the monitor's name or target, any case.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description:
Severity matches an open incident's current severity and a resolved
one's peak severity (how bad it got).
parameters.name: severity

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: The organization's incidents at a glance, for a page header: open incidents by current severity and those nobody acknowledged, incidents resolved in the last 7 days, and the mean time to resolve (opened to resolved) of incidents resolved in the last 30 days. Takes no filters: it describes the organization, not a list view.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: An incident with its timeline and every alert sent for it (with delivery status, so a failing channel shows here).

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

post.description: Marks an open incident as being handled: its reminders stop. Idempotent; a resolved incident is returned unchanged.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: The organization's monitors with their current status, by default ordered by status severity (critical, warning, pending, ok, paused) then name; `sort` picks another order, and a cursor only continues the sort it came from. `status` is the severity of the last conclusive check (an inconclusive one, such as a failed registry lookup, never moves it) and `condition` its reason with facts (days left for SSL and domain monitors). Rows of HTTP monitors have `last24h` (checks by severity, uptime and warning share, approximate p50/p95 over the last 24 full hours plus the current one; no data is absent, not 100%). `include=history` adds each row's newest 60 results (`history`, newest first) for a heartbeat strip. Rows carry no settings; `variant` names what each monitor does (`keyword` for an HTTP monitor that looks for a keyword).

parameters.description:
Include is a comma-separated list of optional row parts: history
adds each row's last 60 check results.
parameters.name: include

parameters.description:
Sort: status (default, by overall status: critical, warning,
pending, ok, paused, then name), name (A to Z), lastChecked (most recent first), uptime
(lowest over last24h first; no data, and SSL and domain monitors,
last), created (newest first).
A cursor only continues the sort it came from.
parameters.name: sort

parameters.description:
Status matches the overall status (the worst of the monitor's status
and its watched aspects').
parameters.name: status

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

post.description: Creates an enabled monitor; its first check runs right away. Every check setting is required.

403.description: Forbidden, or monitor limit reached (LIMIT_REACHED), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

post.description: Applies one action to up to 100 monitors, each exactly as its own request would (pause closes its open incident, resume checks soon, delete refuses a linked monitor with MANAGED_RESOURCE) after an IAM check on that monitor (UpdateMonitor for pause/resume, DeleteMonitor for delete). Not atomic: the answer has one item per id, in request order, ok or the problem code that monitor's own request would have had (NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, MANAGED_RESOURCE, UNAVAILABLE, INTERNAL_ERROR). The request itself fails only when invalid (an unknown action, no ids, more than 100, a malformed or repeated id) or when permissions can't be checked (503). Shares the on-demand check budget (one unit per request).

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

post.summary: Pause, resume or delete many monitors

delete.description: Deletes the monitor and its whole check history. A monitor that belongs to a resource of another service (parentResource set) is refused with 409 MANAGED_RESOURCE: remove it there.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: A monitor with its settings and current status. Secret header values are never returned.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

patch.description: Changes the given fields. A settings object replaces the settings as a whole; omit a secret header's value to keep the stored one. The type can't change, nor the domain of a monitor that belongs to another service's resource.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: How the monitor alerts. useDefaults: alerts go to the organization's default channels (or, with none, its members by email) on down, expiring, expired and recovered, with the default confirmations shown. applicableEvents lists the events monitors of this type can send.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

put.description: Replaces how the monitor alerts: confirmations (failures before an incident opens, successes before it resolves), reminder interval (0: none) and which events go to which channels. An empty routes list sends no alerts. useDefaults: true returns to the organization defaults.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: One entry per UTC day, oldest first, for the `days` days ending today (default and maximum 90): check counts by severity, uptime % ((ok + warning) / conclusive checks) and an estimate of the minutes spent down (HTTP monitors; absent and 0 for SSL and domain monitors), and noData for a day without checks (draw it gray: it is never 100%). Today is refreshed every few minutes.

parameters.description: Days is how many UTC days, ending today, the bar covers (default 90).
parameters.name: days

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: The newest certificate an SSL or HTTPS monitor saw: subject, issuer, SANs, validity, serial, the presented chain and whether it verifies, days left counted from now, and (SSL monitors) the expiry thresholds with the alert window and the next threshold to be crossed. 404 when no check has seen a certificate (plain HTTP and domain monitors never do).

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

post.description: Runs the monitor's check immediately (paused monitors too) and returns the stored result. Billed like a scheduled check; rate limited.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)
No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: The monitor's check history in [from, to), newest first. Defaults to the last 24 hours. Raw results are kept at least 30 days (whole months are dropped once entirely past retention).

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

post.description: Restarts scheduled checks; the next one runs right away. Idempotent.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: Uptime %, latency and a bucketed series for the range ending now (hourly up to 7d, daily beyond). Uptime is (ok + warning) / (ok + warning + critical), HTTP monitors only. Refreshed every few minutes.

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)

get.description: Every time a check moved the monitor to another status, newest first: from, to, when, how long it lasted (endedAt absent and the duration running until now for the newest), and what the check said (condition, statusCode, message). Inconclusive checks never change the status. Each change carries `events`: what else happened while its status lasted, newest first (`certificate_renewed` with the previous and the new certificate, for SSL monitors and HTTP monitors that watch their certificate; no alert is sent for it). Kept a year. Pausing is not a status change (see the audit log).

403.description: No permission for this (FORBIDDEN), or the token's scopes don't allow this (reason INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE)
